title: Small house on posts, from Jim's pencil sketch

reasons.above_grade_mm: the sketch's '?' from grade to the floor; Jim's word gives it
reasons.section_mm: the sketch draws no post size; Jim's choice or a load check gives it
reasons.frost_line_mm: 42 in, Michigan frost depth, research row site.frost_mrc

reasons.thickness_mm: assumed: a 4-1/2 in (114 mm) SIP floor panel, the wall standard's thickness, research row sip.prs610_panel_thickness; Jim's floor build-up gives it
reasons.elevation_mm: the floor's top is the datum the walls and their 12 ft stand on, so its 114 mm panel lies below it

reasons.height_mm: reading: the south elevation's '12' as wall height, floor top to roof underside; 12 ft overall above grade is the other reading
reasons.thickness_mm: a 4-1/2 in (114 mm) SIP wall panel, ANSI/APA PRS 610.1 sec. 4.1, research row sip.prs610_panel_thickness
reasons.panel_width_mm: 4 ft is a sold width (sip.stock.premier_widths, sip.stock.acme_sizes); chosen narrow for handling and take-down; open for ranking

reasons.north_eave_mm: reading: the hatched hangover on the south, 8 ft past the floor; centred, 5 ft each end, is the other reading
reasons.thickness_mm: the sketch draws no rafter or deck; Jim's framing gives it

reasons.band_height_mm: Jim, 2026-10-18: every window is 4 ft by 8 ft, the 8s along the floor
reasons.first_sill_mm: Jim: the first 4 ft of the south wall is a SIP panel below the windows
reasons.south_bands: Jim: two stacked 4x8 windows on the south, the upper one lighting the sleeping loft
reasons.east_bands: Jim, 2026-10-18: only south-facing glass; the east window was the earlier idea

reasons.u_value: assumed: typical double glazing, not chosen by Jim
reasons.solar_heat_gain_coefficient: assumed: typical double glazing, not chosen by Jim
reasons.sun_watt_per_square_metre: assumed clear-sky peak; the solver applies it to every side

reasons.mean_reflectance: assumed mid-grey interior; Jim's wall finish gives it
reasons.glass_transmittance: the BRE standard figure for double glazing as the Camden daylight reports quote it
reasons.sky_angle_degrees: assumed open sky; the site gives it

reasons.wall_r: assumed R-20 for a SIP wall (ft2 F h per BTU); the SIP thickness gives it
reasons.roof_r: assumed R-30; the roof build-up gives it
reasons.floor_r: assumed R-20; the floor build-up gives it
reasons.door_r: assumed R-5 for an insulated door, not checked against a source

reasons.heating_degree_days_f: NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 annual normal, base 65F, station USW00014850 TRAVERSE CITY CHERRY CPTL AP MI, read from the NCEI data service 2026-10-17
reasons.south_glass_sun_btu_per_ft2_season: PVGIS-NSRDB hourly irradiance on a vertical plane at 44.7408 N, 85.5825 W, 2005-2015 average, October to April summed (aspect 0 = south: 506.2 kWh/m2 = 160451 BTU/ft2), gross: no shading, counts sun on days that need no heat
reasons.east_glass_sun_btu_per_ft2_season: PVGIS-NSRDB hourly irradiance on a vertical plane at 44.7408 N, 85.5825 W, 2005-2015 average, October to April summed (aspect -90 = east: 283.2 kWh/m2 = 89761 BTU/ft2), gross: no shading, counts sun on days that need no heat
reasons.west_glass_sun_btu_per_ft2_season: PVGIS-NSRDB hourly irradiance on a vertical plane at 44.7408 N, 85.5825 W, 2005-2015 average, October to April summed (aspect 90 = west: 301.1 kWh/m2 = 95438 BTU/ft2), gross: no shading, counts sun on days that need no heat
reasons.north_glass_sun_btu_per_ft2_season: PVGIS-NSRDB hourly irradiance on a vertical plane at 44.7408 N, 85.5825 W, 2005-2015 average, October to April summed (aspect 180 = north, which PVGIS echoed as -179: 102.5 kWh/m2 = 32480 BTU/ft2), gross: no shading, counts sun on days that need no heat

reasons.fuel_btu_per_unit: Jim: one grown tree is about 20 million BTU, a cord of oak is 24 to 26 million by hobby sources
reasons.boiler_efficiency: assumed 70 percent; sources run 55 to 80 percent

reasons.width_mm: Jim, 2026-10-18: the north door's framing is 4 ft wide by 8 ft tall
reasons.height_mm: Jim: 8 ft tall door framing; a 4 ft tall 8 ft wide SIP panel sits over the door and its neighbour
reasons.offset_mm: open: which end of the north wall the door is at; the west end is a placeholder

reasons.thickness_mm: the subfloor thickness is not banked; the deck thickness waits for the OSB choice
reasons.elevation_mm: Jim: the sleeping loft floor is 8 ft above the living floor

reasons.member_width_mm: a 2x6 is 1.5 by 5.5 in actual, 38 by 140 mm
reasons.member_depth_mm: assumed 2x6; the beam solver says whether it is enough
reasons.modulus_mpa: E = 1.4 million psi for No.2 SPF, NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A, research row lum.nds.fv_spf_no2 (visual-read, not binding); 1.4e6 psi x 0.006895 = 9653 MPa

reasons.live_load_psf: 30 psf for sleeping rooms, research row site.live_sleeping

reasons.min_door_width_mm: 3 ft, Michigan Residential Code 2015 R311.2, research row code.r311_2_door
